resources.string: The whole deck is dealt out. Your goal is to be the first to get rid of every card in your hand.
Lead any set of cards of one rank. Everyone after you must beat it with the same number of cards of a higher rank, or pass.
The 3 is lowest and the 2 is highest. A 2 wins the trick at once, and four of a kind starts a revolution that flips the order.
The first player out becomes President, the last becomes Scum. Next round the Scum hands over its best cards.
Finishing earlier earns more points. The most points after the last round wins the session.
The revolution rule comes from the Japanese version of this game, Daifugo, whose name means Grand Millionaire.
The whole deck is dealt out. Your goal is to be the first to play every card in your hand.
Whoever holds the 7 of diamonds opens with it. Any other 7 can then start a new row for its suit.
Build each row outwards from its 7: play the card one higher or one lower, from the Ace up to the King.
If you can play, you must. If nothing fits, you pass. With the pass penalty on, every pass adds 5 points.
The first hand to empty wins. Everyone else scores the points left in their hand, from 1 for the Ace to 13 for the King.
Sevens is also called Fan Tan, Parliament or Domino, because its rows of cards growing from the middle look like a game of dominoes.
